issues.failure_explanation: Lemma 4.3 (lem4) is applied with X = |s_{tau_i}|^2|r_{tau_i}|^2, so the inner expectation is conditioned on the value of X. The next displayed line silently replaces this by conditioning on tau_i. These conditional expectations differ whenever j -> |s_j|^2|r_j|^2 is not injective, for example when several residual entries are zero or equal. The two outer expectations are still equal by the tower property, because X is tau_i-measurable. But the stated identification of the conditional expectations is false in general, and Lemma 4.3 as stated does not give it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply the tower property directly with sigma(tau_i): E[g(tau_i) Y] = E[g(tau_i) E(Y | tau_i)]. Alternatively, state the conditioning on tau_i in Lemma 4.3.
issues.overall_effect: The inequality of Lemma 4.4 is still true, but the displayed derivation is not valid as written. The result feeds the main theorem and its corollaries.
issues.title: Conditioning on a function of tau_i replaced by conditioning on tau_i in the proof of Lemma 4.4
issues.why_classification: A one-line local fix restores the argument. Every statement, constant and rate is unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the indices in $[m]$ may be even allowed to appear repeatedly in one draw of the batch-sampling $\tau$

issues.failure_explanation: In Lemma 4.4, A_tau and S_tau keep one row per position of tau. The sum over i of |s_{tau_i}|^2|r_{tau_i}|^2 counts repeated indices with multiplicity, so beta^S_{i,j} = max over tau with tau_i=j of ||S_tau A_tau||^2 is computed on the matrix with repeated rows. In a row paving with q = max|T_t|, blocks with |T_t| < q can only be drawn with repeats (Example 3.1 uses tau=(1,1)). There ||S_tau A_tau||^2 = 2||S_1 A_1||^2, not ||S_{T}A_{T}||^2. With q=3 and tau=(2,2,3), the repeated-row norm can be up to 2||A_T||^2. So beta^S_{i,j} does not equal the stated block norm. The inequality D^2 >= S^T B_S^{-1} \hat P S then no longer follows from Lemma 4.4 and Lemma 4.6. The same effective-set versus repeated-row inconsistency appears in the formula for beta^S in Remark 5.4, which uses effective sets while Corollary 5.2 defines beta^S as max over tau.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo Lemma 4.4 with the effective set tau_E: use ||S_{tau_E}r_{tau_E}||^2 = sum over j in tau_E, and weights Pr(j in tau_E) = \hat P_jj. Then define beta^S via effective sets. Alternatively, keep repeated rows and carry the multiplicities into beta^S in Theorem 5.3 and Remark 5.4.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem 5.3 does not establish the claimed B_S and the bound. The final bound is probably still true, since the projection depends only on the effective set. But a different argument is needed. The beta^S formulas of Remark 5.4 and the sharpness comparisons in Remark 5.5 inherit the inconsistency.
issues.title: beta_{i,j}^S identified with the unique-row block norm although tau can contain repeated indices
issues.why_classification: A contained reformulation of one lemma and of the beta definitions fixes it. The method, the form of the bounds and the scope survive, but a nontrivial change of the lemma and its use is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma 4.7 (lem5) is invoked to get (thm4Eq5), which requires nonnegative sample covariance of xi with the squared error norm. The hypothesis only gives nonnegative covariance of xi with the unsquared norm. These are not equivalent. Take xi=(0,0,1,1) and norms (3,0,1.5,1.5): the covariance with the norm is 0, while the covariance with the squared norm is negative (4.5 versus 9). So (thm4Eq5) does not follow from the stated hypothesis.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the hypothesis by Cov(xi, ||x^{(k)}-x_*||_2^2) >= 0, which is exactly what Lemma 4.7 needs.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the hypothesis does not support (thm4Eq5), and hence not (thm4Eq6) or the resulting rate bound. The experimental 'Thm 5.4 bound' also rests on this unverified hypothesis.
issues.title: Covariance hypothesis stated for the norm but used for the squared norm
issues.why_classification: A one-line change of the hypothesis makes the cited lemma applicable. The proof structure and conclusion are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusion (thm4Eq2) compares two deterministic quantities, E||x^{(k+1)}-x_*||^2 and E||x^{(k)}-x_*||^2, with E(xi_tau) and min over S. A 'with probability 1-delta' qualifier is meaningless for it. The proof only obtains (thm4Eq8), an inequality between random sample averages, on the Hoeffding event (probability >= 1-delta) for a fixed S. An inequality that holds only on an event cannot be integrated over the whole space to give the claimed expectation inequality. On the complement the inequality may fail, and no bound controls its contribution. Moreover, a, b, the sample-size condition, the covariance condition and the event all depend on S, yet the minimum over S is taken outside without control. The sample covariance hypothesis is also a random, data-dependent condition used as if it were a fixed assumption. As written, the concentration argument does not prove the stated bound.

failure_location.quote: Taking expectation on both sides of (\ref{thm4Eq8}) leads to the sharper estimate (\ref{thm4Eq2}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either state the result for the sample quantities, as in (thm4Eq8), with probability 1-delta and a fixed S. Or assume a population-level condition Cov(xi_tau, ||x^{(k)}-x_*||^2) >= 0 and conclude the deterministic bound E||x^{(k+1)}-x_*||^2 <= (1 - E xi_tau) E||x^{(k)}-x_*||^2 directly, which makes the epsilon/delta part unnecessary.
issues.overall_effect: The concentration-based 'sharper' bound, a headline claim of the abstract and conclusion and the basis of the 'Thm 5.4 bound' in all experiments, is not established as stated. Its probabilistic form and the epsilon-slack have no valid derivation.
